claims.statement: Triage enumerates the corpus directory non-recursively in sorted order, filtering on canonical extension sets declared in triage.py (PDF_EXTS, TEXT_EXTS, OFFICE_EXTS and their union SUPPORTED_EXTS) which are the single source of truth shared with the parser.

Triage classifies PDFs into scanned, born_digital or mixed from words-per-page and images-per-page thresholds computed with pypdf, and returns the `unreadable` category rather than raising when pypdf cannot open the file at all.
The per-page image count in triage is best-effort by design: it swallows a specific set of pypdf exceptions raised by malformed PDFs and continues with a lower count instead of failing the document.

Triage computes a SHA-256 hash of each file's full bytes, but no consumer currently reads that field; content-level duplicate detection is instead performed separately over extracted text in the corpus redundancy stage.

The PDF extraction chain is layered so each level covers the failure mode of the one before: Docling out-of-process first, falling through on any exception to pdfminer text plus pdfplumber typing, then to a pdfplumber-only extraction, and finally to an empty ParsedDoc.
The parsing chain never raises: the terminal except branch returns an empty-markdown ParsedDoc at confidence 0.0 rather than propagating, making an unreadable document a result rather than an error.
All extracted text passes through NFKC compatibility normalization, which flattens ligatures and other compatibility forms while leaving French accented letters unaffected.

Both pdfplumber extraction paths call page.flush_cache() after each page because pdfplumber retains the parsed object cache of every page it touches, which would otherwise exhaust memory on documents of several hundred pages.

A font-mapping failure produces text that is present in volume but unreadable — (cid:NNN) tokens or Unicode replacement characters — which length- and structure-based confidence measures cannot detect; cid_failure_fraction measures the share of text occupied by these artifacts to expose it.

Above a cid-fraction threshold the chain attempts a pdfplumber re-extraction, and _better_extraction adopts it only if it STRICTLY reduces the cid fraction, keeping the primary result on equal fractions; the attempt is wrapped so a failing re-extraction leaves the primary intact.

parse_confidence is a blend of a saturating length component and the ratio of text-bearing blocks, then capped when characters-per-page fall below a floor (catching a parser silently losing some pages), capped again when the pdfplumber fallback was adopted, and finally multiplied by (1 - cid_fraction) so a half-unreadable document cannot report high confidence.

On the Docling path fallback_used is always False when confidence is computed, even if per-batch pdfminer fallback fired inside the Docling extraction, so the fallback confidence cap never applies to a Docling-parsed document and degradation there surfaces only through the cid penalty and the per-page cap.

The legacy chain assembles markdown with [[IMAGE:p=..;idx=..]] placeholders inserted in reading position, with images sorted by vertical position within each page, which is what lets enrichment substitute descriptions back at the correct location.
doc_id is derived from the filename stem, so two corpus files differing only by extension collide on document identity and on output filenames.

Non-PDF input is classified by extension alone before any PDF inspection, into `text` for plain-text formats and `office` for .docx/.pptx; `unsupported_format` remains for any other extension and is reachable only by calling triage_file directly, since the directory walk filters on SUPPORTED_EXTS.

parse_document no longer accepts a category argument and takes only `path` positionally; every other parameter is keyword-only, which prevents a caller silently binding a stray positional argument to `pages` — the exact failure that removing the previously-unread category parameter would otherwise have caused at its two positional call sites.

The triage category is now genuinely consumed, but by the run orchestration to route the unsupported-format case rather than by the parser — classification decides whether to attempt extraction, not how to extract.

Plain-text formats are parsed and scored like any other document via a dedicated path that reads the file, applies the same NFKC normalization and splits on blank lines into text blocks, requiring no PDF machinery and no additional dependency.

Plain text is decoded as utf-8-sig with errors="replace", so decoding damage becomes U+FFFD replacement characters which cid_failure_fraction already counts — penalising parse_confidence and flagging a mis-decoded text file through the same mechanism built for PDF font-mapping failures rather than letting it pass as clean.

A text ParsedDoc traverses the remaining pipeline safely because pages is None, which disables the per-page confidence cap, and its empty image list makes enrichment a no-op; a test asserts a text document never reaches Docling, pdfminer or pdfplumber.

Word and PowerPoint documents are extracted directly by _docx_extraction and _pptx_extraction, dispatched by extension in _direct_extraction before the parser setting is consulted, so neither format reaches Docling, pdfminer or pdfplumber; a test asserts this by making all three raise.

The Word extractor walks the document body's XML children in order rather than reading the paragraphs and tables collections separately, so a table keeps its position in the extracted text instead of being appended at the end.
Word heading levels are carried into the extracted markdown as `#` prefixes rather than flattened into plain paragraphs, because the structure criteria are scored on the markdown.
PowerPoint speaker notes are included in the extracted text, guarded by slide.has_notes_slide, so prose a RAG system would ingest enters the quality verdict rather than being dropped.

Tables from both office formats are rendered as markdown pipe tables and typed as Block(kind="table"), and pictures as Block(kind="image"), so the deterministic scorers see an office document with the same block vocabulary as a PDF.

Office extraction emits no ImageRef at all: ImageRef carries PDF-point geometry read by the enrichment cropper, and neither python-docx nor python-pptx exposes anything comparable, so images are counted as blocks without being located.

Triage reports the real slide count as `pages` for a .pptx and None for a .docx, because pages feeds the per-page density cap in parse confidence and Word pagination is a renderer artefact python-docx cannot report.
A .pptx whose slide count cannot be read degrades to pages=None and keeps the `office` category rather than being pre-judged unreadable at triage, leaving the unreadable verdict to the parser.

A corrupt office file makes the extraction dispatch raise, which parse_document catches to return an empty-markdown ParsedDoc at confidence 0.0 with an unreadable block, so the file lands as `unreadable` rather than propagating an exception.
